Economic claim: A sleeve above its own ten-month moving average earns its equal share of the budget and a sleeve below it holds cash. Zero fitted parameters anywhere in the weights, so this is the floor every other rule must beat after costs to have earned its complexity.

The same trend gate, but budget is allocated inversely to each sleeve's trailing volatility rather than equally. The claim is that volatility is the one moment forecastable at this sample size and that timing it beats naive diversification net of the turnover it adds.
Citation: Kirby and Ostdiek (2012); Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen (2012)

Economic claim: The gate is the sign of the trailing twelve-month total return rather than position against a ten-month average. That is a different economic statement about persistence horizon, not a reparameterisation: the two states disagree on roughly a fifth of sleeve-months, most of them at turning points.
Citation: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012); Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen (2017)
